note: Known divergences that a check SEES, PRINTS, and does not fail on -- each one a decision somebody made on a date, with a date it stops being in force. Read by scripts/acknowledgements.py; see that module's docstring for the rule. The short version: the thing that expires is the ACCEPTANCE, never the finding. Before review_by the check is green and the item is counted in the summary line; after review_by the check is RED on 'this acceptance expired', which is a red a human can always close by deciding something. This file lives at the repo root and NOT under public/, because public/ is rsynced to production and this is CI metadata.
how_to_add_an_entry: Every field in scripts/acknowledgements.py REQUIRED_FIELDS is mandatory and non-blank, and `check` must appear in `checks` below -- the loader REFUSES the whole ledger otherwise, rather than skipping the entry, because a skipped entry reads to the next person as a real finding. Pick review_by per entry from when you actually expect to know more; do not give every entry the same date, or they all come due at once and the honest answer becomes a bulk re-accept, which is the same as having no clock.

policy.source: Chosen in PR ci/acknowledgement-clock (2026-08-09) as two working weeks -- long enough that the accepter sees EXPIRING SOON before the cliff and can act deliberately, short enough that the warning is not background noise. Not derived from measurement; revisit if warnings start being ignored.

checks.check-encoding-safety: scripts/check-encoding-safety.py -- the cp1252 preamble and encoding= sweep. Keys are repo-relative module paths, matching Finding.path.
checks.check-art-staleness: scripts/check-art-staleness.py -- art this repo UPLIFTED from pdoom1, held against data/art-register.json (generated by scripts/build-art-register.py). Keys are <code>:<path relative to public/> for per-image findings, and <code>:mirror or <code>:<count name> for whole-register ones. Codes: S1 a deployed image whose upstream verdict is not `keep`; S2 the mirrored verdict has moved (needs a pdoom1 checkout); S3 the bytes changed under an unchanged filename; S4 roster drift; S5 deployability drift; S6 the mirror is older than its declared max age; S7 an expired human origin assertion; S9 the register's summary disagrees with its own records. UNKNOWNs (U1-U4) are NOT findings and never appear here -- an acknowledgement tolerates a divergence, and 'we could not tell' is not one.
checks.check-campaign-facts: scripts/check-campaign-facts.py -- the _facts_this_copy_must_not_break blocks in content/campaigns/. Keys are <campaign file>::<fact id> for entry-scoped findings, and <campaign file>::<finding name> for findings against the copy as a whole. NOTE: the `human` tier's review clock is NOT here -- it lives inline in the campaign file, next to the fact, because the person who acts on it reads that file and nothing else. This ledger holds only findings the check reports and somebody tolerates.
checks.validate_data: scripts/validate_data.py -- the data-contract and integrity sweep over public/data and public/leaderboard/data (schemas, encoding, weekly-league freshness and key agreement, published-board consistency, seed-file census). Keys are the row `name`, e.g. 'league:freshness' or 'board:published_key'. Only FAIL rows can be acknowledged: a WARN already prints without blocking, so acknowledging one would buy nothing and cost a clock nobody reads.

acknowledgements.what: A deployed image whose upstream verdict is 'discard'. public/assets/icons/events/action_funding_grant_proposal_v2_128.png is uploaded by every deploy of public/. Its upstream asset gen:game_icons:action_funding_grant_proposal:v2 carries verdict 'discard' in pdoom1 tools/art_review/review_state.json, recorded 2026-08-14T12:05:58Z. The two sibling icons in that directory carry 'keep' and are unaffected.
acknowledgements.why: TWO IN-REPO SOURCES DISAGREE AND NEITHER IS THIS SEAT'S TO OVERRULE. pdoom1's art_prompts/batch_2_actions_and_ui.yaml:116 says selected_variant v2, and #283 copied that into PROVENANCE.json on 2026-08-07 in good faith -- the human review that discarded v2 happened a week LATER, on 2026-08-14, and nothing connected the two. So this is not a mistake in #283; it is the exact rot this register was built to detect, caught on its first run. The remedy is a production removal (rsync --delete makes a delete from public/ an unpublish, and an exclude would NOT achieve it -- an exclude protects the uploaded copy), and which source governs 'what art ships' is a cross-repo question. Harm is bounded and measured, not assumed: no page, stylesheet, script or markdown file in this repo references the icon -- the only mention anywhere under public/ is its own PROVENANCE.json sidecar -- so a reader reaches it only by guessing the URL. That is the #283 precondition without the #283 harm; #283's damage was six REJECTED variants sitting beside three chosen ones with nothing to tell them apart, and here the register now tells them apart in writing.
acknowledgements.accepted_by: pdoom1-website seat, PR feat/art-register. NOT Pip's ruling -- he has not been asked, and the ruling needed is his. This entry is what asking looks like when the asker cannot wait and must not act unilaterally on another repo's decision record.
acknowledgements.on_expiry: Do not bulk re-accept, and do not delete this entry without doing one of the three. (1) Rule that the human review governs: delete public/assets/icons/events/action_funding_grant_proposal_v2_128.png, remove its entry from PROVENANCE.json, rebuild the register, and remember the file stays live on DreamHost until that deploy runs. (2) Rule that the generation spec governs: fix pdoom1's review_state.json or its art_prompts YAML so the two sources agree, then rebuild -- the finding clears itself. (3) Rule that a discarded variant may ship while nothing links to it, and re-accept with that reason written down and a new review_by. All three close it; none is a shrug.

The rollover is not stalled -- it is PARKED (.github/workflows/weekly-league-reset.yml, PARKED 2026-08-24, PARKED-UNTIL 2026-09-02), deliberately, to keep an unattended league rollover off main.
acknowledgements.why: THE FINDING IS TRUE AND THE REMEDY IT NAMES WOULD BREAK THE BOARD. The check assumes the site's league week should advance on a calendar. Under the (seed, ladder_version) key model it must not: the seed comes from the SHIPPED CLIENT and changes only when a new build ships. v0.14.4's release_manifest.json carries league_seed weekly-2026-w35, and that is what the site publishes. MEASURED, not assumed: weekly-league-manager.py --status reports it would open week 2026_W36 on a DERIVED seed (weekly_2026_W36_4810cf21), so running the rollover today would publish a board no shipped client posts to -- the key mismatch that stranded 23 submissions, recreated in the week Pip is inviting EAGx attendees to play. Being ~10 days old is currently CORRECT BEHAVIOUR. The property that actually matters -- does the site's key match the shipped client's -- is measured by check-epoch-drift.py, which is GREEN: both sides on (weekly-2026-w35, L6). This is acknowledged rather than fixed tonight because the real fix is to the CHECK, and rewriting a blocking data-contract gate deserves a reviewed change rather than a fast one.

acknowledgements.on_expiry: Do NOT close this by running the rollover -- see `why`; that is the one action that makes it worse. Close it by one of: (1) fix the check so freshness is measured against key agreement with the shipped client rather than the calendar age of current.json, and drop the '(seed, game_version)' language at validate_data.py:213 which encodes the superseded key model; or (2) a new pdoom1 build ships carrying a new league_seed, after which a rollover matched to it is correct and clears this honestly; or (3) re-accept with a new date and say which of those is being waited on. Option 1 is the durable one.
